newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Grain - U.S. soymeal moves into price window.
newsitem.headline: China Grain - U.S. soymeal moves into price window.

text.p: Soymeal from the United States has become far more attractive to Chinese buyers as South American and Indian-origin meal prices rise, oilseed traders in Hong Kong and China said on Thursday.
"Lately South American meal and Indian meal prices have gone up significantly enough that they are comparable to U.S.-origin soymeal prices," said a senior oilseeds trader in Hong Kong.
He said his firm was discussing the sale of 30,000 tonnes of U.S. low-protein soymeal with Chinese buyers, but that Chinese bid prices, at $310 a tonne C&F, were still too low.
"It's all talk at the moment," he said.

Current offers for U.S. soymeal are at about $330 a tonne C&F China, while South American soymeal was quoted at around $310-$315 C&F. China is said to be in the market for Indian soymeal at between $320-$325 a tonne.
A China-based source reported a client interested in 40,000-50,000 tonnes of U.S. soymeal at $305 FOB New Orleans.

"Adding $40 per tonne for shipping and a three percent import duty, it translates to about 3,950 yuan ($355) per tonne, which would be reasonable for high protein," he noted, adding that the client would buy if it were available.
Another Hong Kong-based trader reported a cargo of U.S. soymeal sold to China a week or so ago at about $315 a tonne C&F Shanghai for October delivery.
"It's a combination cargo of 30,000-50,000 tonnes of U.S-origin beans and meal being shipped together," the source said, noting the vessel had yet to leave the United States.
A dip in Chicago soybean prices earlier this week, on an improved outlook for the U.S. crop, may have provided a window of opportunity for sales to China, one grain trader said.

"I believe one or two Panamax cargoes of U.S. soybeans were traded, when the market moved to about $7.85 a bushel a couple of days ago," the source said, adding they were for late October or November delivery, and were sold in the low $320s C&F China. The U.S. Department of Agriculture said on Monday that as of Sunday the U.S. soybean crop was 55 percent good to excellent, up from 53 percent the previous week.
The China National Grains and Oils Information Centre reported domestic number two soybean prices in Jilin at 3,150 yuan ($380) a tonne on Wednesday, unchanged from last week.
China-based traders put the domestic price of soybeans slightly higher at between 3,200-3,300 yuan ($385-398) a tonne.
Trading in soybeans and soymeal at the Dalian Commodities Exchange has been brisk, industry sources said.
About 130,000 tonnes of soybeans -- some from the United States and some domestic -- would be delivered at the exchange in September against futures contracts, said an official at the exchange.

"At the futures exchange, speculators who play the game can force the other party to deliver, so they then have to buy the cargo and some of it is imported and some is from within China," explained a Chinese trader.
But traders are keeping an eye on China's soybean harvest, expected in soon.
"New soybeans from this year's harvest should be on the market in the autumn," the Future's Herald newspaper said earlier this month.
The traditional Chinese mid-autumn moon festival, to be celebrated this weekend, marks the end of the autumn harvest season.
